title: Hopf bifurcations and period-doubling cascade in a two-delay predator–prey model with Holling type II response
task: Characterize bifurcation dynamics and route to chaos in a two-delay predator–prey model
key_results: Hopf bifurcations with alternating criticality organized by Bautin bifurcations; complete period-doubling cascade (periods 2→4→8→16→32) with Feigenbaum ratio δ ≈ 4.6692 converging to universal value; accumulation point at τ₁^∞ ≈ 18.64 marking transition to aperiodic oscillation
comments: This is ecological dynamics, not biophysics per se, but the mathematical analysis of delay-induced bifurcations is technically rigorous and may inform understanding of temporal dynamics in biological regulatory networks.

model_io.model: Two-delay Holling type II predator–prey system (DDE)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Maturation and conversion delays generate stability switching and bistability via Hopf bifurcations
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: sequence of subcritical/supercritical Hopf bifurcations observed with fold of periodic orbits producing bistability

hypotheses.hypothesis: Period-doubling cascade follows classical Feigenbaum route to chaos
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: empirical Feigenbaum ratios converge to δ ≈ 4.6692; accumulation point at τ₁^∞ ≈ 18.64 marks onset of complex dynamics
